title: Palo Alto Networks research, as relayed by Cyber Security News, describes vishing and adversary-in-the-middle attacks used to reach Microsoft cloud, OneDrive and SharePoint data
date_note: Cyber Security News page gives only its publication day; the underlying Palo Alto Networks report was not read.
geo_basis: Unit 42 research relayed by the article; no victim location stated; pin at the United States
summary: Cyber Security News, summarizing Palo Alto Networks research, reports that callers posing as IT support sent employees to lookalike sign-in pages. It says the Vortex cluster enrolled an unauthorized MFA device and Cinder reused a persistent session token, with mailbox, OneDrive and SharePoint data collected. It says Cinder sent extortion messages.
plain: Cyber Security News, citing Palo Alto Networks, says phone scams and fake sign-in pages let attackers into Microsoft accounts without cracking MFA, after which they took cloud data and sent extortion messages.
exec: Cyber Security News, citing Palo Alto Networks, says staff phone scams can lead to unauthorized MFA devices and theft of cloud files and mail from Microsoft accounts.
action: Cyber Security News says organizations should require employees to verify unexpected support calls through a help desk number they already know; Palo Alto Networks is cited as advising phishing-resistant MFA and browser extension allowlists.

validation.note: Only Cyber Security News was read; the Palo Alto Networks report itself could not be found in search, so the cluster names and details are unverified against it.

review.note: stronger than the source: removed Com-affiliated and attributed MFA enrollment, token reuse and extortion to the clusters the article names
